    State of Good Repair Program

    On this page

          In 2015, House Bill 1887 was passed and incorporated into the Code of Virginia (§ 33.2-369) to create the State of Good Repair (SGR) Program. Also, Code of Virginia (§ 33.2-232) and Code of Virginia (§ 33.2-214) have requirements regarding the SGR program. 

          Known as State of Good Repair (SGR), the program provides funding for deficient bridges and pavements owned or maintained by the Virginia Department of Transportation and or localities, as approved by the Commonwealth Transportation Board (CTB).

          The CTB approved a revised State of Good Repair Prioritization Process in July 2024 to guide the prioritization and allocation of funds.

          State of Good Repair funds are allocated by the Board to projects in all nine construction districts based on a priority ranking system that takes into consideration (a) the number, condition, and costs of bridges with a general condition rating of no more than five for at least one major bridge component and (b) the mileage, condition, and costs to replace deteriorated pavements, and further provides that the Board shall ensure an equitable needs-based distribution of funding among the highway construction districts, with no district receiving more than 17.5 percent or less than 5.5 percent of the total funding allocated in any given year.

          State of Good Repair - pavement

          The State of Good Repair (SGR) pavement program provides funding for deteriorated pavement owned or maintained by the Virginia Department of Transportation or localities, as approved by the Commonwealth Transportation Board. 

          Important dates

          Virginia localities must submit applications for SGR Primary Extension through the SMART Portal. The application period typically opens the first week of October and closes by mid-December each year. A notification of the application period is sent to eligible localities each year.

          There are two certifications that must be acknowledged in the Smart Portal. The Maintenance of Effort Certification in which localities certify funds received are in addition to and do not replace their current funding level and the Federal Certification in which localities acknowledge projects must be developed using federal guidelines and any funding received will be federal. In addition, a Detailed Project Cost Estimate is required to be uploaded with the primary extension applications.

          State of Good Repair - bridges

          The State of Good Repair (SGR) bridge program provides funding for NBI bridges in poor condition or in fair conditions with a minimum general condition rating equal to 5 (hereafter referred to as “cusp" bridges) condition that are owned by the Virginia Department of Transportation and/or localities.
                      
          Project scopes should be established to preserve, reconstruct, or replace damaged or deteriorated elements in the most practical and cost-effective manner and include measures (materials, technologies or details) to mitigate future deterioration.

          SGR bridge projects are selected using a multi-variable formula. The formula addresses a wide variety of factors to select projects that will provide the best value over the life cycle of the treatment.

          • Bridge Prioritization Formula
          • Smart Flags

          • For scope eligibility requirements see IIM-S&B-95.
          • According to § 33.2-369 of the Code of Virginia, SGR funds are to be used for “…reconstruction, replacement, and other improvements anticipated to extend the useful life by at least 10 years…” A table of minimum actions that will provide at least 10 years of additional service life for cusp structures can be found in Chapter 32 of the Manual of the Structure and Bridge Division, FILE NO. 32.06-2

          Pre-scoping documents must be submitted for full applications as outlined below. Details of requirements for pre-scoping documents can be found in the “SGR Bridge Pre-Scoping Document Requirements” section below. All applications will be reviewed in accordance with requirements outlined in IIM-LD-260 / IIM-IID-11, titled “Project Application Review.”
             
          For localities:

          • This year, SmartPortal will not be used for locality SGR bridge applications.
          • Instead, all applications are to be submitted directly to the VDOT district locality liaison and district bridge contacts.
          • Full applications are required for all eligible structures to be considered for SGR bridge project selection
          • Pre-applications are no longer required

          Application submittal requirements for SGR bridge funds: Projects With Extensive Work Scopes:
          The following documents must be submitted at the time of application for bridge projects with work scope that includes bridge replacement, superstructure replacement, deck replacement, bridge widening, or any other significant work with a project estimate totaling more than $10 million.:

          • Pre-Scoping Report Narrative
          • Proposed Smart Flags, if applicable
          • Conceptual Drawings or Sketches
          • Project Cost Estimate(s)  
            • Project Estimate Summary (PES) with backup information for the recommended alternative (the Cost Estimate Workbook (CEWB) has been phased out in favor of the PES. See the “SGR bridge pre-scoping document requirements” below for more information on the PES).
            • *Full SGR structure replacement estimate
            • *Other estimates as required by Chapter 32, Section 2 (alternative analysis)

          Application submittal requirements for SGR bridge funds: Projects With Less Extensive Work Scopes:
          For bridge projects that do not contemplate widening or component replacement, an SGR Fair (5) Intake Form can be filled out instead of providing a pre-scoping report narrative and conceptual drawings. The SGR Fair (5) Intake Form does not need to be filled out for projects requiring a Pre-Scoping Report Narrative. 
           
          * For a project alternative that is not the recommended project scope:
          The estimate does not need to be completed using the PES but can be a cost estimate created by other means. Additional project estimating tools can be found at VDOT’s Cost Estimation Website. Please provide backup information about how the estimate was completed and what the estimates are based on.  

          Pre-scoping documents must be submitted prior to the deadline. The submittal documents must include the following elements and conform with the requirements of IIM-LD-260 / IIM-IID-11, titled “Project Application Review.”

          Application submittal requirements for SGR bridge funds: Projects With Less Extensive Work Scopes:
          For bridge projects that do not contemplate widening or component replacement, an SGR Fair (5) Intake Form can be filled out instead of providing a pre-scoping report narrative and conceptual drawings. The SGR Fair (5) Intake Form does not need to be filled out for projects requiring a Pre-Scoping Report Narrative.

          1. A pre-scoping report narrative that includes the following elements as appropriate:

          • Project description
          • Scope justifications
          • Significant Scope Elements (Specifically include how scope is eligible for SGR bridge funding per S&B-IIM-95.)
          • Scope elements not eligible for SGR (address items not eligible for SGR. Immediately contact district to advise how such elements will be funded.)
          • Alternative analysis (use the repair/preservation, rehabilitation or replacement decision process as outlined in Chapter 32 of the Manual of the S&B Division.)
          • Risk assessment (Worksheet template and guidance document)
          • Proposed smart flags
          • Discussions of significant scope items such as: 
            • Bridge configuration
            • Features carried (including approach roadway tie-in points, alignment, profile, and cross section)
            • Features intersected (road, water, railroads, clearances)
            • Geotechnical (roadway, bridge)
            • Maintenance of traffic (detour, offset alignment, part-width-construction)
            • Traffic
            • Right-of-way and utility impacts
            • Hydrologic and hydraulic requirements
            • Environmental impacts and permits
            • Stakeholders
            • Bicycle-pedestrian features
            • Constructability issues
            • Complex project elements
            • Project concerns associated with the following documents:
              • Manual of the S&B Division, Part 1, Design Exceptions / Waivers / Approvals
              • Chapter 6 of the Manual of the S&B Division (Sections 4 and 9)
              • IIM-LD-235, titled “Common Sense Engineering (CSE) and Context Sensitive Solutions (CSS)”
              • IIM-LD-255 (Practical Design Flexibility in the project development process) Chapter 6 of the Manual of the S&B Division (Sections 4 and 9)

          2. Conceptual drawings or sketches:

          • Proposed plan view of structure and approaches (include limits of structure, approach road tie-in points, and maintenance of traffic).
          • Existing and proposed cross sections of deck.
          • Existing cross section of immediate approach roadway (show dimensions of lanes and shoulders, and guardrail).
          • Proposed section of immediate approach roadway (show dimensions of lanes and shoulders, and guardrail).

          3. Project cost estimates

          • Fill out and submit a Project Estimate Summary (PES) for the SGR-funded portion of the work, developed in accordance with the VDOT Cost Estimating Manual and VDOT Project Management Procedure IIM-PMO-3.7 
            • Project Estimate Summary (PES)
            • Project Estimate Summary (PES) Key Features
            • Project Estimate Summary (PES) Training Video
          • If any of the project’s scope items will be funded by other (non-SGR) sources, indicate these scope items and their associated costs clearly in the cost estimate. 

          4. Documentation to Support use of Smart Flag(s)
              See Virginia Structure Priority Formula for documentation requirements. 

          5. Locality Application Form

          • Fill out the "Locality Application Form"
          • Be sure to sign and date the "Locality Acknowledgement" at the bottom of the form.

          The application requirements for VDOT-owned bridges are the same as for locality-owned, except submittal documents will be uploaded to the “01-New Submittals and Comment Resolution Sheet” folder for the project in ProjectWise.

          The pre-scoping document requirements for VDOT owned bridges are the same as for locality owned projects, except of course the "Locality Application Form" is not required.

          Funding Request:

          • For projects (SGR Bridge, Bridge Formula, CTB Formula Bridge) exceeding allocated funding, district bridge engineers or project managers must request additional funding from the Infrastructure Investment Division (IID) following published guidelines.
          • Scope Verification:
            • Required for SGR Bridge and Bridge Formula funded projects to ensure cost increases are not due to ineligible work.
            • CTB Formula Bridge projects do not require scope verification.

          No Significant Change in Scope:

          • District bridge engineer must email the Central Office Bridge Management Team (CO BMT (Ryan Bowler, Ryan Edwards and Alan Johnson)) at key milestones.
          • Email should confirm that the project scope remains as originally approved.
          • Include the district bridge engineer or designee's name.
          • Please use the following template on these emails:

          CO Bridge Management Team,

          The updated project cost estimate for UPC XXXXX now exceeds the existing allocation, and the district is coordinating with IID for additional funding. This email is being provided to confirm that the scope of the project is consistent with the original scope that was approved at the time of project selection.

          (District Bridge Engineer or Designee Name)

          Significant Change in Scope:

          • District bridge engineer contacts CO BMT to discuss new scope items.
          • An email is then submitted confirming that additional scope items have been reviewed and are necessary and eligible for SGR funds.

          Application to Locality and VDOT-Owned Projects:

          • The same process applies.
          • The district bridge engineer certifies the scope on behalf of the locality and may request additional information.

          Copy IID on Emails:

          • Please Include Infrastructure Investment Division (Jason Robinson and Craig Ahlin) on scope verification emails, as they decide on additional funding.
